answer: Under density-locked birth-registry admission, each newcomer's key derives from proof-of-work seeded by hashing its three nearest registered identities, so a mass attacker forging clustered sybils hits difficulty equal to prior births under that same triplet: the first identity costs 2^18 hashes, the tenth costs 2^26. Honest agents spread across the map pay the base 2^18 once, since neighborhoods stay sparse and no kernel of dense registration forms around them. Fake agents cannot hollow out cost by relocating, because each forge attempt re-seeds from the very density it creates.
